verdict: Avoid new unsecured or greenfield exposure in Krishnagiri fruit and vegetable processing; lend only to established pulp/frozen processors with contracted offtake, and then on tight working-capital structure.
title: Krishnagiri Fruit & Vegetable Processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Krishnagiri and Dharmapuri cultivate mangoes across 51,000 hectares, and 24 mango pulp industries sit in Krishnagiri alone [3]. The unit buys seasonal fruit at harvest, crushes it into pulp or freezes it, stores it in cold rooms, and sells to beverage, dairy and export buyers across the year. **Cash is made in the crush season and consumed in the eleven months after it** — so the loan is really financing inventory, not a factory. Raw material is the largest cost line and moves with the crop [9]; the ICRA note on a gherkin processor makes the same point — yield and price swing with weather and hit margin directly [8].

## Where value and cash sit now
Pricing power is thin and realisation-led. The listed peer Foods & Inns saw Q4 profit fall 16% to ₹19 crore even as margin improved to 6.6% from 5.8%, with realisations down 25.3% on Middle East disruption to cash flows [4]. **Volume growth is not the same as cash growth here.** India-wide exports are down 9.6% Apr-to-date in USD [D], so the export leg of pulp demand is soft; when a proposal leans on export realisations, ask for the buyer-wise contract and the last twelve months' actual realisation per tonne — collect from customer.

## The local picture and the growth opening
Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap [D] — the local trade is billing less. Against that, the state has proposed five integrated mango processing parks with cold storage and pulp units in Dharmapuri-Krishnagiri [1][2], and farmers have welcomed a value-addition centre [3]. **That is a proposal, not a built asset — treat it as a pipeline signal, not collateral.** The peer's frozen segment grew about 39% YoY in Q2 FY26 [6] and snacks and pulp are showing strong growth with capacity expansion underway [7]. So pursue established frozen and ethnic-snack processors and pulp units with domestic beverage buyers; avoid new entrants waiting on the park, and avoid pure export pulp traders.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the season: cash credit sized to peak inventory, repaid at the tail of the crush, not a term loan for a shed. **Take stock and receivables statements every month, and insurance on inventory as a condition.** Where the park is cited as the plan, ask for the allotment letter and the promoter's own equity before sanctioning anything. Bank credit is running +26.3% YoY against output +5.1% [D]; the system is lending ahead of production, so our exposure must be earned by the borrower's own cash cycle.

## Early warning signs
- Monthly stock statement showing inventory ageing past the normal sale window (monthly) -> stop fresh drawdown and inspect cold storage.
- Realisation per tonne falling two quarters running (quarterly) -> reprice limit to actual cash cycle.
- GST returns showing billing below the sanctioned turnover estimate (monthly) -> ask for buyer-wise sales register.
- Any single buyer crossing a third of sales (quarterly) -> seek assignment of receivables or reduce limit.
watch: Inventory ageing beyond normal sale window -> freeze drawdown, physical inspection
Billing below estimate for two months -> ask for buyer-wise sales register
Two consecutive quarterly falls -> resize limit to actual cash cycle
Single buyer above a third of sales -> seek receivables assignment or cut limit
Park allotment and promoter equity (on proposal)
No allotment letter or thin equity -> decline the greenfield request
